MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  POLICY DEVELOPMENT / STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION
  MARCH 12, 2022

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
at 9:08 a.m. on the Council Chambers patio, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR
ZERUNYAN.

1.  FLAG SALUTE

2.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Zuckerman**

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development/PW Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  AVENU INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS PRESENTATION ON PROPERTY TAX TRENDS,
  SALES TAX OUTLOOK AND BUSINESS LICENSE ADMINISTRATION

Administrative Services Director Whitehead introduced Tom Adams and Laura Burnett of Avenu
Insights & Analytics, who provided an update on the current state of the City’s Sales Tax, Property
Taxes and Business Licenses, including:

  -  Current Sales Tax Performance
  -  Los Angeles County Pool: Use Tax
  -  Sales Tax Revenue Forecast
  -  Property Tax Allocation & Forecast
  -  Business license Administration Update
  -  Discovery Recovery Services
  -  Revenue Summary for 2022

Discussion ensued about the impact of the pandemic on sales tax.

Discussion ensued about the business license process and challenges, with direction to provide
the City Council with monthly reports for the processing time of business licenses to provide
accountability and transparency to the community.

**COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN joined the meeting at 9:45 a.m.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered this item to be received and filed.

B.  KNN PUBLIC FINANCE PRESENTATION

City Manager Grammer introduced Mark Young of KNN Public Finance, who presented a
comprehensive analysis of the City’s CalPERS Unfunded Accrued Liability, reviewed the City’s
long-term strategy, and advised the City to adopt a City policy regarding the funded percentage of
the CalPERS Unfunded Accrued Liability.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered this item to be received and filed.

DRAFT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 12, 2022 (PDS)
 MAYOR ZERUNYAN called for a recess at 10:45 a.m.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN reconvened the meeting at 11:08 a.m.

C.  PRESENTATION BY KATHLEEN MCGOWAN, ENVIRONMENTAL/STORMWATER
  CONSULTANT

City Manager Grammer introduced Kathleen McGowan of McGowan Consulting, who provided an
update on the funding of the City’s stormwater Capital projects, the Torrance Airport project, the
Machado Lake Watershed and Drywells projects, Palos Verdes Peninsula Multi-benefit Flow
Diversion, Palos Verdes Drive East stormwater redevelopment and the Marloma project.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered this item to be received and filed.

4.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  MID-YEAR REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

City Manager Grammer reported that the attached mid-year reports were provided from each
department regarding the status of activities at mid-year (FY 2021-22).

Administration Department mid-year report provided by Assistant City Manager Davis (as per
the agenda material).

Administrative Services Department mid-year report provided by Director Whitehead (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development & Public Works Department mid-year report provided by Director
Wahba (as per the agenda material).

Community Services Department mid-year report provided by Assistant City Manager Davis (as
per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE MID-YEAR REPORTS.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN called for a recess at 12:20 p.m.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN reconvened the meeting at 12:45 p.m.

B.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the items presented and prioritize them
  on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

ADMINISTRATION DEPARTMENT

  AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA) PROPOSED EXPENDITURE PLAN

  City Manager Grammer and Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to approve the
  proposed ARPA expenditure plan, directing staff return with a more detailed grant
  program for local non-profit organizations and small businesses in the coming
  months.

  ELECTRIC BICYCLES

  Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).
DRAFT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 12, 2022 (PDS)
   Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to update the City’s
  Municipal Code to define and permit electric bicycles and include provisions for
  speed limits, and for staff to explore educational/outreach programs.

  OUTDOOR SMOKING PROHIBITION

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council direct staff to work
  with “Kick Ash” and Behavioral Health Services and other groups to develop an
  educational outreach campaign focused on voluntarily restrictions on outdoor
  smoking at commercial centers and potentially gaining support for future City
  regulation of such areas.

  COYOTE AND PEAFOWL MANAGEMENT

  Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  obtain services with Los Angeles County for additional coyote management
  beyond the City’s existing coyote management program.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  consider modifying the current peafowl management program to charge the City’s
  cost ($200 per bird) to the person requesting each permit, consider limiting the
  number of birds per request, and return to the City Council with an updated
  program.

  FIREWORKS

  Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  return to the City Council with options to impose stricter penalties and fines, and
  to get a quote from the Sheriff’s Department in the cost of utilizing Fire Suppression
  Units.

  EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT

  Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  SOLID WASTE/RECYCLING UPDATES

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  FISCAL HEALTH REPORT, FY 2010-11 THROUGH FY 2019-20

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

DRAFT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 12, 2022 (PDS)
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF,
  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE FISCAL HEALTH REPORT.

  There being no objection, MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

  FINANCE UPDATE

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  FINANCE UPDATE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY UPDATE

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT & PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT

  PLANNING POLICY ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION:

  Building & Safety Services

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material), outlining the consideration of moving Building & Safety services
  from Los Angeles County entirely to Willdan.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council move Building &
  Safety Services from Los Angeles County, all to Willdan, as summarized in the staff
  report, and for staff to obtain a Task Order and scope of services from Willdan to
  effectuate this change effective July 1.

  PUBLIC WORKS POLICY ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION:

  Road & Sidewalk Repairs

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material), outlining the concerns of response times and costs with the current
  use of Los Angeles County Department of Public Works (LACOPW) for large roadway
  pothole repairs/patches and sidewalk, driveway apron, handicapped ramps, and curb and
  gutter repairs.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  meet with Hardy & Harper for their pricing strategy and also conduct an RFP from
  other similar companies, all of which pay prevailing wages.

  Commercial District Improvements

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  return at a future meeting with the conceptual plans for commercial district
  improvements that was prepared in the early 2000s, to be revisited and discussed
  further in deciding how to move forward.

  Stormwater Programs Update

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material), providing updates on planning for stormwater capital projects, the
  Torrance Airport Stormwater Basin Regional Project, Distributed Stormwater Retention

MARCH 12, 2022 (PDS)
   via Dry Wells and future funding pursuits. He also provided an update on the following
  Supplemental/Future Stormwater Projects: Palos Verdes Peninsula Multi-Benefit Flow
  Diversion Project, Harbor City Park Multi-Benefit Stormwater Capture Project, Rolling
  Hills Road Green Street and Palos Verdes Drive East Green Street/Redevelopment.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  PUBLIC WORKS PROJECTS UPDATES:

  Street Re-Surfacing & Sidewalk Repair Projects

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  Dapplegray School and PVDN Intersection Improvements

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  Rolling Hills Road Improvements

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  Stormdrain Repair Program

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  Local Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP)

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  Metropolitan Water District (MWD) Re-Lining Project

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  Butcher Park

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  It was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to continue moving forward
  with the plans and specifications for the park, inform the residents of the additional
  delays, and include images of the planned park emphasizing the importance of the
  infrastructure work being done by MWD.

DRAFT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 12, 2022 (PDS)
   Nature Center

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  Marloma Septic to Sewer Project

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  COMMUNITY SERVICES PROJECT UPDATES:

  Nature Center Update

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to bring this item
  back for future discussion and consideration.

  Other Capital Projects

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  outlining other park capital projects identified to be considered over the next few fiscal
  years.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  PARKS AND RECREATION PROGRAM OVERVIEW:

  Assistant City Manager Davis and Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a
  staff report (as per the agenda material), providing an overview of league sport field
  usage, tennis operation review, contract recreation class overview, class registration,
  proposals and contracts, fees, park usage and City parks and rights-of-way water
  conservation.

  This item is informational for the Council. It was the consensus of the City Council
  to move forward with CalWater on the proposed turf removal program at Highridge
  Park and City Hall.

5.  ADJOURNMENT

At 3:12 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the adjourned City
Council meeting scheduled for Tuesday, March 15, 2022 at 12:00 p.m. on the Council Chambers
Patio at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates,
California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Frank V. Zerunyan
City Clerk  Mayor

DRAFT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 12, 2022 (PDS)
